disease_label_per_paper: High-risk pulmonary embolism presenting with recurrent syncope and shock
presentation_summary: 69-year-old woman initially had syncope with gait disturbance and no chest distress, chest pain, dyspnea, or other respiratory symptoms.
Admission vitals included heart rate 68/min and blood pressure 146/64 mmHg; initial D-dimer was 0.44 ug/mL, BNP 46 pg/mL, and troponin 0.12 ng/mL.
She had recurrent syncope with palpitation and then developed shock on May 9, 2021, with blood pressure 87/60 mmHg.
On the shock day D-dimer rose to 6.19 ug/mL and troponin rose to 0.97 ng/mL; bedside Doppler showed pulmonary hypertension and lower-leg intermuscular venous thromboses.
CTPA showed multiple emboli in the pulmonary artery and its branches; she received rt-PA thrombolysis and later rivaroxaban.

quality_warnings: This case is a post-initial-imaging PE test: CTPA, Doppler evidence, shock physiology, D-dimer, and troponin are rankable.
